## Problem

Several deterministic bot micro-simulations are knife-edge calibrations: a subtle, legitimate gameplay tweak (e.g. the 1-5% gentler thrust-press reduction in AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A) flips their outcomes because scores are dominated by discrete hit/bullet collisions.

During AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A two tests had to be recalibrated:
- src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts - synthetic human seed moved 7 -> 14.
- src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts - RUN_SEED moved 0x0b07 -> 0x0b16.

On the base behaviour, src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts already regressed on 13/24 seeds, and the competent-vs-legacy AC6 test only wins in base because the legacy bot chaotically collides with bullets; without bullets the legacy bot scored higher (22 vs 20) on base.

## Goal

Make these tests robust rather than seed-picked:
- Aggregate competence/style comparisons over a set of seeds (e.g. assert the styled/competent bot is not systematically worse), or
- Compare on scenarios whose score is not dominated by discrete collisions.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The style-match AC4 demonstration no longer depends on a single lucky seed (e.g. asserts over multiple seeds).
- AC2: The competent-vs-legacy AC6 test asserts an objective-based advantage rather than relying on chaotic bullet collisions.
- AC3: Recalibrating either test is not required by an unrelated small bot-feel tweak.
- AC4: Full test suite, typecheck and build pass.

## Problem

`node_modules/.vite` accumulates orphaned `deps_temp_<hash>` directories whenever a Vite dep optimisation is interrupted or collides — at intake there were 98 (141 MB), now **95 dirs / 158 MB total in `node_modules/.vite`**. They are pure cache debris: each is a partially written pre-bundle. The epic's AC3 timing work is unaffected functionally, but the debris wastes disk, slows directory scans, and is evidence that dep optimisation is re-running/colliding (which is one source of the transform/import variance measured in AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG).

## Why this was not fixed inline

`node_modules` is **shared by every worktree on this host via symlink**; deleting the cache while another agent's suite is mid-run can corrupt that run. The producer rule 'never destroy another agent's work' applies, so the cleanup needs a safe, quiescent mechanism rather than an opportunistic `rm -rf`.

## Expected change

A small, documented, safe cleanup path — e.g. `scripts/clean-vite-cache.mjs` that:
- refuses to run when any `vitest`/`vite` process is alive (or requires `--force`),
- removes only `deps_temp_*` (never the valid `deps/` bundle or `deps_ssr`),
- reports bytes reclaimed, and
- is documented in `docs/dev/test-suite-timing.md` (cache-hygiene section) and optionally wired into `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** A read-only `--dry-run` (default) reports the orphaned `deps_temp_*` count and bytes; `--apply` removes only those dirs and prints the reclaimed bytes.
- **AC2:** The script refuses to delete while a `vitest`/`vite` process is running unless `--force` is passed, and is covered by tests (dry-run classification, refusal path) that do not require a real cache.
- **AC3:** Documentation states why the cache is shared across worktrees and why the quiescence guard exists.
- **AC4:** After `--apply` on an idle host, `npx vitest run --project unit` still passes (cache regenerates cleanly).

## References

- AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG — measured the transform/import cost and rejected the optimizer/isolate/pool variants; notes the collision evidence.
- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` — the existing periodic hygiene report this could extend.
data.title: Vite dep-cache hygiene: 95 orphaned deps_temp_* dirs (158 MB) in node_modules/.vite

# Align AI_Hell's test framework with the Tableau-Card-Engine game repos

AI_Hell runs a bespoke Vitest setup: `vitest.config.ts` + `vitest.projects.ts` with a
static classifier (`classifyTestFiles` / `isIntegrationTest` in `vitest.projects.ts`)
splitting test files into `unit` / `integration` projects, and test roots `src/`,
`scripts/`, `vite/` — there is **no top-level `tests/` directory**. Every sibling TCE
game repo (and the scaffold template `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`) uses the
standard layout: a `unit` project in `vite.config.ts` with
`include: ['tests/**/*.test.ts']` and no per-file classifier.

**Goal:** bring AI_Hell's test layout and project selection into line with the sibling
repos so cross-repo conventions, agent/audit tooling expectations (top-level `tests/`
tree), and the test skill's type profiles apply uniformly.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No test lost or doubled.** After migration, AI_Hell's full suite runs the
   identical set of `*.test.ts` files currently selected by
   `vitest.projects.ts::allTestFiles` (src/, scripts/, vite/) — same count and same
   per-file project membership; verified by a before/after selection diff.
2. **Standard layout adopted.** Tests live under a top-level `tests/` tree laid out to
   match sibling repos (e.g. `tests/deploy/` for infra guards, `tests/<area>/`),
   selected via the standard include globs in `vitest.config.ts` (or the config file's
   `test.projects`), with `tsconfig.json` including `tests/**/*.ts`.
3. **Isolation preserved.** Phaser/DOM-booting tests retain their separation from the
   fast node `unit` project (the deliberate unit/integration split — parent
   AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV, blocked child AH-0MVF6XV87001NSEJ). Alignment must NOT flatten
   Phaser-heavy tests into the node unit project or regress suite runtime. The
   `src/test/projectMembership.test.ts` guard is updated to assert the new layout and
   still passes.
4. **Tooling keeps working.** The test skill's per-type profiles
   (`.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json`, `.pi/test-config.json`) remain
   functional — update only if project names/commands change, and verify each type
   (`unit`, `coverage`, `e2e`) runs.
5. **Documentation updated.** Comments in the vitest config(s), AGENTS.md and any
   dev notes reflect the new layout. CHANGELOG.md excluded (ship skill).
6. **Full suite passes** with the changes.

## Constraints

- Refactor only — no change to app behaviour.
- Preserve the deterministic membership guard pattern (`vitest.projects.ts` is
  deliberately the single source of truth for selection; keep an equivalent guard).
- This item may also relocate `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts` (added by the watch-ignore
  port, MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0) into `tests/deploy/` for full parity — sequence after or
  alongside that port.

## Related work

- MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0 — Port Vite watcher-ignore to sibling game repos (discovering item; adds `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts` under the current layout)
- AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV — parent of the unit/integration split decision

- AH-0MV53ABBU008FKE0 — Test-skill runner no-ops: no .pi/test-config.json suiteCommands for vitest (completed)

# Background scenes

> One-line headline: give each campaign level its own NASA space-photo background, swapped on level change with an unmistakable "warp" transition (hyperspace-style).

## Problem statement

The game currently renders all combat on a solid black backdrop (`GAME_BACKGROUND_COLOR = '#000000'`), so the space setting is implied only by the neon vector art and every level feels visually identical. This work bundles a pool of NASA space photos and displays a distinct background per level, transitioning between them with an explicit "warp" effect so level changes are unmistakable and the campaign feels like travelling deeper through space.

## Users

- **Player (primary):** "As a player, I want to see a different space background on each level and a warp transition between them, so moving to a new level feels like a jump through space and the run stays visually engaging."
- **Developer / capture pipeline:** "As a developer, I want deterministic background selection (same level → same background) so unit tests and recorded demo/capture video stay stable and repeatable."
- **Producer / reviewer:** "As the producer, I want the level-change transition to be unmistakable (the same standard already applied to phase-shift/wormhole effects, see AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU) without hurting gameplay readability."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. At least 20 NASA space photos are bundled as game assets (public-domain / NASA-approved media) with attribution and licence notes; backgrounds render at the full 960×540 canvas (Phaser FIT scaling) and are a non-interactive layer that never occludes gameplay or intercepts input.
2. Each campaign level — the 10 levels in `LEVELS` (`src/waves/Formations.ts`) — gets a distinct background chosen **deterministically** from the pool via a level→background manifest; the background changes exactly on level change (the existing `levelCleared` → next-level path in `PlayScene._handleWaveEvent`), not per wave.
3. A "warp" transition effect plays while backgrounds change — timed to the existing `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` (1.5 s) transition pause — after which the new level's background is fully shown; the effect is deterministic, time-boxed, and does not block input or wave progression.
4. Gameplay readability is preserved: backgrounds are dimmed/desaturated beneath the neon vector art so enemies, bullets and the player ship stay legible (GDD §7.1 aesthetic, "2.5× keeps bullets legible against the neon background").
5. Background creation/swap logic lives in the shared combat core (`src/scenes/core/`) consumed by `PlayScene` and the gyms (gym↔game parity convention in AGENTS.md); any gym divergence is documented.
6. Tests cover: deterministic level→background mapping, swap fires on level change (not wave), warp effect activates during the transition and completes within its duration, and the background layer does not intercept input; document updates (README, code comments, credits/attribution file with licences, GDD §3.2/§7.1 references as needed); the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Bundle, do not fetch at runtime.** Images are committed as repo assets (mirrors the existing `public/audio` precedent) — **confirmed by producer (2026-10-25)**. No runtime NASA API calls — avoids CORS, offline flakiness, and non-deterministic tests/demos.
- **Size/performance:** raw NASA photos are multi-megabyte; compress and resize to ≤ 1920×1080 (2× for HiDPI) JPG/WebP so the added bundle stays modest (target ≲ a few MB). Warp must use bounded, disposable effects (exported tuning constants + tracked/cleaned-up display objects, following the existing `ENDOFRUN_ENABLE_*` pattern).
- **Licensing/attribution (producer emphasis, 2026-10-25):** NASA media are generally US-government public-domain works, but record **attribution and licence** per image; ship a credits/attribution file (`ATTRIBUTION.md`) listing each photo's source, title, and licence.
- **Level-change hook:** reuse the existing `WaveManager` → `PlayScene._handleWaveEvent` ('levelCleared') → `_announceLevel`/`_startTransition` path (`LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS = 1.5`).
- **Parity convention (AGENTS.md):** shared behaviour lives once in `src/scenes/core/`; do not fork copies into `PlayScene` and the gyms.
- **Language consistency:** keep the warp visual language consistent with the existing wormhole/phase-shift VFX (`src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts`, `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts`).
- No new runtime dependencies; prefer Phaser built-ins (tweens, particle emitter, camera effects) for the warp.

## Existing state

- Solid black background configured in `src/core/constants.ts` (`GAME_BACKGROUND_COLOR = '#000000'`), `src/core/gameConfig.ts`, and `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` (`backgroundColor`).
- 10 campaign levels in `src/waves/Formations.ts` (`LEVELS`), each with a theme `name` (Entry, Descent, The Core, Firestorm, … The Gauntlet) surfaced in the HUD progress label (`PlayScene._progressLabel`).
- Level changes flow: `WaveManager` emits `levelCleared` → `PlayScene._handleWaveEvent` → `_announceLevel()` + `_startTransition()` (1.5 s pause, `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS`). The transition banner and wave-timer visibility already ride this path.
- Existing warp-adjacent visuals: `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts`, `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts`; open item AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU (make phase-shift/wormhole effects unmistakable) is related work.
- No image-asset pipeline: the only image asset is the MenuScene GitHub-logo data URI; audio assets live in `public/audio`. Vite `base: './'`.

## Desired change

- Add ≥ 20 compressed NASA space photos under `public/assets/backgrounds/` plus an attribution/licence file; a new level→background manifest (e.g. `src/data/backgrounds.ts`) maps each level index to a texture key.
- Shared core (`src/scenes/core/`) owns background lifecycle: create the dimmed backdrop at a negative depth below gameplay on scene create, destroy on shutdown, and swap on level change.
- Warp effect (`src/vfx/backgroundWarp.ts`): triggered at the level-change transition — hyperspace-style one-shot (converging streak overlay + radial scale distortion + brief flash/crossfade into the new background), its phases and total duration testable and tied to `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS`.
- Deterministic selection (same level number → same background) keeps tests and captured demo videos stable — **confirmed by producer (2026-10-25)**.

## Key Files

- `public/assets/backgrounds/` — bundled NASA photos (≥ 20, compressed) + `ATTRIBUTION.md` (source, title, licence per image).
- `src/data/backgrounds.ts` (new) — level→background manifest, texture-key registry, deterministic selection helper, warp config constants.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` (or `CombatCoreScene.ts`) — shared background create/swap/warp lifecycle so `PlayScene` and gyms match.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — wire the level-cleared transition to background swap + warp trigger; background cleanup on shutdown/restart.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` (+ affected gym scenes) — parity verification / documented divergence.
- `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.ts` (+ test) — the warp transition (or extend existing wormhole/phase-shift visuals).
- `src/core/constants.ts` — dimming/warp tuning constants.
- Docs: `README.md` (assets/credits), `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§3.2 level themes, §7.1 aesthetic) and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 (gym parity note) as needed.

## Related work

- **AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU — Make Phase Shift and wormhole-emergence effects unmistakable** (open). Related: warp transition effects must meet the same "unmistakable" bar; coordinate visual language (`related-to:AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU`).
- **AH-0MV8BQ75V005QNZ1 — Make the background of the level/wave banner semi-transparent** (completed). Related: the transition banner and HUD live above the new backdrop; contrast must remain readable (`related-to:AH-0MV8BQ75V005QNZ1`).

### Related work (automated report)

- **AH-0MTBTP6K3002YMAA** – Reset thrust flame length to 0 when the pressed keys change (completed)
- **AH-0MVFBCVIS007BN81** – implement.py: behind-only child worktree mis-detected as 'has changes' and auto-finished (in-progress)
- **AH-0MU72YVFR005VB2N** – Create Main Menu scene (completed)

Repository file matches: `README.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` (weak/generic keyword matches).
Full report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-AH-0MVIB7PD50029ZY1.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Repo size:** adding ~20 compressed photos grows the repo by roughly a few MB — acceptable for the web-first distribution model (GDD §6.3); keep compression targets explicit.
- **Visual variance:** NASA images vary in composition; choose dark, space-dominant shots and apply a dim/desaturation overlay so neon gameplay stays legible.
- **Attribution/licence:** NASA media are public-domain, but attribution and licence must be recorded per image — ship `ATTRIBUTION.md` and reference it in docs (producer confirmation, 2026-10-25).
- **Warp readability risk:** too subtle repeats the "not unmistakable" producer complaint (AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU); too strong hurts playability. Mitigate with exported tuning constants and an early in-`PlayScene` review; keep the effect time-boxed to the transition window.
- **Low-end performance:** full-screen distortion/particles must be bounded and cleaned up (registry destroyed on shutdown like other VFX layers).
- **Scope-creep guard:** opportunistic extras (animated starfield, parallax layers, per-level colour grading, menu/GameOver backgrounds, runtime NASA fetch) are recorded as separate linked work items — not this item's scope.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

This item was auto-dispatched to intake (herdr downtime worker, 2026-10-25); no interactive interview was possible, so the three decisions below were initially drafted as documented assumptions flagged OPEN QUESTION. The producer answered all three on 2026-10-25 — answers recorded here as final.

- Q1: "Should the NASA photos be downloaded and committed into the repo, or fetched at runtime from NASA APIs?" — Answer (producer, 2026-10-25): **"1. bundle (be sure to record attribution and license)"** — bundle the photos as committed repo assets, recording attribution and licence per image. Research: `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts` loads a data-URI; no runtime network-image pipeline exists; bundling mirrors `public/audio`. Final: **bundle; no runtime fetch.**
- Q2: "What exactly should the 'warp' effect look like? — A: hyperspace-style one-shot transition (converging streak overlay + radial scale distortion + brief flash/crossfade), B: reuse existing wormhole/phase-shift VFX, C: instant swap with flash." — Answer (producer, 2026-10-25): **"2. A"** — **hyperspace-style one-shot transition**, timed to `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` (1.5 s). Final: **Option A.**
- Q3: "How should ≥ 20 photos map onto the 10 levels? — A: one distinct deterministic background per level (pool ≥ 10; surplus as spares/alternates), B: random pick per run." — Answer (producer, 2026-10-25): **"3. deterministic"** — **one distinct deterministic background per level** from the pool. Final: **Option A (deterministic).**

### Source references

- Work item seed description (AH-0MVIB7PD50029ZY1); dispatch comment AH-C0MVNZ6LHD00784U7; producer answers via interactive reply recorded in comment AH-C0MVNZKBYE006VBQT (2026-10-25).
- NASA media usage guidelines (public-domain works; attribution requested) — see [NASA Media Usage Guidelines](https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/).

## Plan (2026-10-28)

Seven child items decompose this epic into vertical slices, created in **test-first dependency order**. Every slice ships its own tests (written before the implementation), and the test-first contract slice lands first. Full-suite gating is left to the dev-push gate; no ad-hoc full runs during implementation.

| # | Child | Type | Effort/Risk | Depends on |
|---|-------|------|-------------|------------|
| 1 | Deterministic background manifest and selection (**AH-0MVSEASIM005TU95**) | task | S / Low | — |
| 2 | Bundle NASA backgrounds with attribution (**AH-0MVSEB2WZ000MZY8**) | feature | M / Medium | 1 |
| 3 | Shared background layer in combat core (**AH-0MVSEB7SA004B26C**) | feature | M / Medium | 1, 2 |
| 4 | Hyperspace warp transition VFX (**AH-0MVSEBCNC005G7XW**) | feature | M / High | 1 |
| 5 | Swap backgrounds on level change with warp (**AH-0MVSEBW8L009O3JD**) | feature | M / High | 2, 3, 4 |
| 6 | Gym parity for background layer (**AH-0MVSEC0J0004YNJC**) | feature | S / Medium | 3 |
| 7 | Document backgrounds, credits and parity (**AH-0MVSEC4RS003KQGV**) | docs | S / Low | 2, 5, 6 |

Parent-AC coverage: AC1 → slices 2 (bundling/attribution) + 3 (full-canvas non-interactive layer); AC2 → 1 (deterministic mapping) + 5 (change on level change only); AC3 → 4 (warp module) + 5 (timing/non-blocking); AC4 → 3 (dim overlay/readability); AC5 → 3 (shared core) + 6 (gym adoption/divergence); AC6 → tests in every slice + 7 (docs + full-suite gate). ## Goal

Crash resilience for dev telemetry: with the dev JSONL sink moving to an in-memory per-run buffer (AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3), a page reload or crash mid-run loses the un-uploaded tail. Streaming telemetry batches to the dev server during the run — instead of one run-end upload — bounds that loss to at most one flushed batch (~64 records, ~1.3 s of play) and removes the page-reload regression that localStorage previously masked.

## Context

- Parent/related: discovered-from:AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3 (in-memory dev sink; this item is explicitly deferred there).
- Current flow: the JsonlTelemetrySink buffers records in memory, flushes batches of 64 to the sink, and the whole run is POSTed once at run end (`uploadDevTelemetry`). A crash before that POST loses the entire run's telemetry; a reload also loses the buffer entirely once it is no longer localStorage-backed.
- Dev only: the same reasoning applies to the production remote sink, which already streams batches via `HttpTelemetryTransport` (with retry/backoff), so production is not affected.

## Proposed design

- Send each flushed batch to the dev endpoint as it is produced (`POST /api/telemetry/upload`) instead of (or in addition to) the run-end upload.
- The server (`vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts`) currently stores each upload as one complete `session-<stamp>.jsonl` and runs the automatic evaluation per upload; a per-batch POST would create many tiny recordings and repeated evaluations. The endpoint (or a new `part` protocol) must therefore either:
  - append JSONL records to the run's open session file keyed by a run id/seed, and evaluate once at run end, or
  - keep the run-end upload and add a lightweight "heartbeat/checkpoint" mechanism that only recovers the tail on demand.
- UX/offline: batches sent while the dev server is unreachable should stay in the memory buffer (or a bounded queue) and be retried at run end; at most one batch may be lost on a hard crash.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A mid-run crash/reload followed by a run-end state loses no more than one flushed batch (~64 records / ~1.3 s) of telemetry; the rest is recoverable from the dev server.
- AC2: The server session file for a run contains its records exactly once (no duplication from partial + final uploads), and the automatic evaluation still runs once per run.
- AC3: Dev CLI tooling (`record-session`, `capture-gameplay`, `verify-dev-telemetry`) continues to work unchanged in behaviour.
- AC4: Full project test suite passes.

## Status

Open decision item — parked until the in-memory sink (AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3) lands. Do not implement concurrently with that item in the same worktree.

# Implement the Music System defined by the Audio Design Chapter

## Goal

Build the runtime background-music system for AI Hell against the fixed design contract captured in
`docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` (produced by **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)**).

User story: *As a player, I want a dynamic, retro-arcade soundtrack that responds to combat intensity, so
that runs feel like the relentless survival experience the game is aiming for; and as a developer I want the
music engine driven by a documented parameter/state contract, so behaviour is testable and reproducible.*

> **Scope stance:** this is **future scope, out of MVP** (GDD §8). The MVP ships baked ToneForge SFX only
> (GDD §7.3), and §7.3 remains authoritative for SFX. This item must **not** be started until the design
> chapter exists and has been reviewed, and it must **not** promote music into the MVP without an explicit
> producer decision.

## Background

- AI Hell currently has **no background music** by design: GDD §7.3 keeps music out of MVP scope, and the
  player-fire grid is deliberately quantised to a **silent internal 80 BPM beat** (AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B).
- SFX are build-time baked WAV assets rendered deterministically by ToneForge and played through Phaser's
  shared `AudioContext` (`src/audio/effects.ts`); the authoritative cue catalogue is
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`.
- The Audio Design Chapter specifies the musical identity (Phrygian Dominant combat scale, Lydian ambient
  scale, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), instrumentation palette, dynamic-mixing rules, state-driven
  transitions, parameter mapping, audio budget and accessibility requirements.

## Expected behaviour and outcomes

- A music system that plays layered/stemmed music driven by an explicit game-state parameter, with
  bar-boundary transitions, stingers, and ducking, as specified by the chapter.
- Music state follows gameplay (e.g. menu/attract, wave combat, boss, low-health tension, run end) with the
  transition rules and timings given in the chapter, and never disrupts the beat grid or the SFX mix.
- Reproducible, deterministic behaviour suitable for automated tests; no audio regressions to the shipped SFX
  pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Contract traceable to the chapter:** every implemented music state, transition, stinger and mixing parameter traces to a named section of `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md`, recorded in a mapping table in the implementation docs.
- [ ] **AC2 — Musical content matches the documented identity:** the delivered cues/stems use the chapter's scales, motifs and progressions (Phrygian Dominant combat, Lydian ambient, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), verified by an explicit audit table (motif → scale degrees → usage state).
- [ ] **AC3 — State machine implemented and tested:** transitions occur only at the documented boundaries (bar boundaries unless a stinger cut-in is specified), with unit tests covering each transition in the chapter's transition matrix, including invalid/reset paths.
- [ ] **AC4 — Dynamic mixing implemented:** ducking, per-layer volume targets and the priority tiers behave as specified; SFX intelligibility is preserved (music ducks under key SFX cues) and is covered by tests.
- [ ] **AC5 — Autoplay and accessibility compliance:** no audio before a user gesture (`AudioContext` resume discipline, GDD §7.3); the chapter's accessibility requirements (e.g. music/SFX independent volume, mute, and any reduction options) are implemented and documented.
- [ ] **AC6 — Budget met:** the shipped music respects the chapter's audio budget (memory, streaming, polyphony, layer count) on the supported targets, measured and recorded.
- [ ] **AC7 — Docs updated:** GDD §7.3 and §8 are updated to reflect the shipped music system, and `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` is marked as implemented for the sections that ship.
- [ ] **AC8 — No SFX regression:** the existing ToneForge baked-SFX pipeline and cue catalogue remain unchanged and their tests pass; any chapter §6.4 procedural SFX recipes are explicitly **not** adopted unless decisioned separately.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project build and test suite pass.**

## Constraints

- **Blocked by** the docs item **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — this item
  must not begin before `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` exists.
- Music stays **out of MVP scope** until a producer decision promotes it (GDD §7.3, §8).
- Keep the gameplay SVG/vector aesthetic and retro-arcade palette of the chapter; UK English in all docs.
- §7.3 (baked ToneForge SFX) remains authoritative for SFX; the chapter is an addendum whose §6.4 procedural
  SFX recipes are design reference only.
- Prefer reusing the existing audio plumbing (`src/audio/effects.ts`, shared `AudioContext`, manifest-driven
  playback) over introducing new runtime dependencies; any middleware adoption (the chapter's FMOD/Wwise
  guidance) is a separate decision — the web build currently has no middleware.

## Approach (indicative)

1. Confirm scope with the producer (MVP vs post-MVP) and record the decision on this item.
2. Ingest the chapter into an implementation mapping table (state → parameter → cue/stem set → transition).
3. Decide the delivery mechanism (baked stems via ToneForge + `AudioContext` playback, per the existing
   pipeline) versus a runtime synthesiser; record the trade-off before coding.
4. Implement the music state machine and mixing layer behind a single facade, mirroring the existing SFX
   façade style; add unit tests per transition and per mixing rule.
5. Add accessibility controls and the autoplay guard; verify budget and measure on target hardware.
6. Update GDD §7.3/§8 and the chapter's implemented-sections marker.

**Key Files:**
- `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` — the design contract (prerequisite)
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — existing SFX façade / shared `AudioContext` plumbing to reuse
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — where combat-state music parameters would be driven from
- `src/core/rules.ts` — game-rules config (including `beatBpm`) that music tempo must stay coherent with
- `src/audio/` — new music module + tests
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 and §8 updates

## Risks & assumptions

- **Overlap with the shipped silent beat grid (medium):** player fire is quantised to an internal 80 BPM beat.
  Music must be tempo-coherent with that grid or the two will fight; assume music tempo is either locked to
  `beatBpm` or documented as intentionally independent.
- **Chapter/SFX divergence (medium):** the chapter's §6.4 procedural SFX recipes differ from the shipped baked
  catalogue; §7.3 stays authoritative (AC8).
- **Middleware assumption (low):** the chapter's FMOD/Wwise guidance is forward-looking; no middleware exists in
  the web build, so it is design intent only.
- **Scope creep into MVP (medium):** music is out of MVP; promotion needs an explicit producer decision.

## Related work

- **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — prerequisite; produces the design contract.
- discovered-from:AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W
- GDD §7.3 (SFX, authoritative for MVP), GDD §8 (Future Scope — "Background music"), and
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` (SFX cue catalogue).
- Beat grid / timing context: AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B (beat-aligned fire grid), AH-0MV01HNLU008S5E3 (beat-timed
  explosion accents).

# Intake brief — Mini-Boss rewards become valuable (AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD)

## Headline

Replace the mini-boss reward choice with a **spin-the-wheel** that always
delivers a guaranteed permanent upgrade: one bonus slot upgrades everything,
5 slots upgrade 3 picks, 10 upgrade 2, and the remaining 84 upgrade 1 — so a
mini-boss victory always makes the build meaningfully stronger.

## Problem statement

Mini-boss rewards currently offer a flat menu (upgrade any one owned item, or
unlock one locked weapon) which reads as a low-value chore rather than a
reward. The player wants a moment of anticipation that *always* pays out in
power, presented as a wheel of fortune spin over the power-ups the player has
invested in permanent slots.

## Users

- **Player (core loop):** after defeating a mini-boss, expects a celebration
  and a guaranteed, tangible power gain.
- **Demo/attract bot:** must not stall on the wheel; auto-spins after the same
  human-like delay as the hold-full choice (AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F contract).

### Example user story

> As a player, when I defeat a mini-boss, I want to click a button to spin a
> wheel showing the power-ups in my permanent slots, watch it slow to a stop,
> and receive the landed upgrade(s) — so the reward feels like a gamble that
> always pays out, not a to-do list.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Defeating a mini-boss opens a **wheel overlay** (the multi-option
   upgrade-or-unlock choice is gone): one wedge per **owned permanent kind**
   across the shared six-slot pool — power-up kinds **and** weapon drops —
   plus a single **bonus** wedge; play is paused exactly like the hold-full
   choice.
2. Spinning is player-initiated (click/keyboard), the wheel animation starts
   fast and eases out (building tension; the outcome must not be predictable
   until it stops), and the landed wedge is highlighted and applied exactly
   once.
3. The spin outcome follows the **100-slot distribution**: 1 slot = bonus
   (every owned permanent kind +1 level), 5 slots = 3 upgrades, 10 slots = 2
   upgrades, 84 slots = 1 upgrade. Multi-upgrade slots pick **distinct**
   owned kinds where possible and repeat a kind only when there are fewer
   owned kinds than the slot's count (a player with one owned power-up landing
   a 3-slot gains +3 levels on it).
4. **Empty-owned fallback:** when the player owns no permanent kinds at a
   mini-boss defeat, the wheel is not shown and the existing hold-full-style
   three-option choice is offered instead, so a mini-boss always pays out.
5. The run-scoped weapon-unlock feature and its reward options are **removed**
   from mini-boss rewards (locked-pool option builders, `getUnlockedWeapons`
   and the checkpoint's `unlockedWeapons` field; `CHECKPOINT_VERSION` bumped
   so stale checkpoints are rejected cleanly).
6. Outcomes are drawn from the **run-seeded RNG** (no `Math.random()`), the
   distribution/resolver and the reward application live in shared modules the
   game and gyms both consume, and demo mode auto-spins after
   `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` so the attract bot never stalls.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the change (GDD §4.4.4,
   `docs/BALANCING.md`, checkpoint notes), including code comments.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes, including unit
   tests for the slot distribution/outcome resolver and PlayScene wheel-flow
   tests replacing the current upgrade-or-unlock reward tests.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity** (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1): slot distribution and reward
  application must live once in shared modules consumed by `PlayScene` and any
  gym surface; no scene-private divergence.
- **Code-first visuals:** icons come from the existing code-drawn
  `src/powerups/icons.ts` (`drawPowerUpIcon` / `drawWeaponIcon`); no external
  art assets (GDD §7.2).
- **Seed reproducibility:** run-seeded RNG only; deterministic tests.
- **Launcher-agnostic overlay:** a single optional selection/result callback
  (mirroring `MineralChoiceScene`'s `onSelect`), so any launcher can drive it.
- No ad-hoc full-suite runs during implementation (test-slot policy); changed
  scope is run via the test skill.

## Existing state

- Defeating a mini-boss fires `_fireMiniBossDefeatHooks` → `openMiniBossReward`
  (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`), which offers **one** upgrade-or-unlock choice:
  every owned permanent weapon/power-up level-up offer (built by
  `buildOwnedLevelUpOptions`) plus every still-locked weapon from
  `MINI_BOSS_LOCKED_WEAPONS` (`src/powerups/unlocks.ts`). The overlay is the
  shared `MineralChoiceScene`; selection applies `applyMineralChoiceReward`
  (`src/powerups/choiceReward.ts`, re-exported by
  `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts`). Rewards are applied exactly once
  (`selectMiniBossReward` resets the open flag). See GDD §4.4.4
  (AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH).
- **Note (stale description):** the description's "choice of 5 random power
  ups" does not match current behaviour — the live reward is the
  upgrade-or-unlock menu described above; the wheel replaces *that*.
- Each wheel-relevant decision is a permanent kind in a **shared 6-slot pool**
  (`src/powerups/slots.ts`) covering both power-up kinds and weapon drops;
  `PowerUpLevelStore` (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`) tracks permanent vs
  temporary levels and per-kind caps; the checkpoint
  (`src/core/checkpointStore.ts`) persists weapon/power-up levels and
  `unlockedWeapons` (the latter is removed by AC5).
- Demo mode already auto-selects the reward via `_randomDemoRewardIndex()`
  after `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` (`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`) — reuse this
  seam for auto-spin.

## Desired change

- New pure module (e.g. `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts`): the 100-slot
  distribution (1 bonus / 5 triple / 10 double / 84 single), a weighted
  outcome resolver over owned permanent kinds, distinct-kind multi-upgrade
  selection (repeats only when fewer kinds than picks), cap-aware handling,
  injectable RNG.
- New launcher-agnostic overlay (e.g. `src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts`): one
  wedge per owned icon plus the bonus wedge, pointer, fast-starting/eased-out
  spin, landed-wedge highlight, click/keyboard to spin, result callback.
  Register in `src/core/gameConfig.ts`.
- Rework `PlayScene.openMiniBossReward`/`selectMiniBossReward`: launch the
  wheel with the owned permanent kinds (from `resolveSlotState`/
  `getWeaponLevels`/`getPowerUpLevels`), apply the resolved outcome once
  through the shared reward machinery, fall back to the three-option choice
  when nothing is owned, and keep demo auto-spin.
- Remove the unlock feature (`src/powerups/unlocks.ts` locked-pool state and
  option builders, `PlayScene.getUnlockedWeapons`, the checkpoint
  `unlockedWeapons` field) and bump `CHECKPOINT_VERSION`.
- Update GDD §4.4.4, `docs/BALANCING.md` and checkpoint docs.
- Replace the current upgrade-or-unlock reward tests in
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`; add deterministic unit tests for the
  distribution and outcome resolver.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — rework `openMiniBossReward`/`selectMiniBossReward` to the wheel flow; fallback; demo auto-spin; drop unlock state.
- `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts` (new) — pure 100-slot distribution + weighted outcome resolver, distinct-kind picks, caps.
- `src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts` (new) — launcher-agnostic wheel overlay: wedges, spin + ease-out animation, pointer, result callback.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — reuse `drawPowerUpIcon`/`drawWeaponIcon` for wheel wedges.
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` — owned permanent kinds feeding the wheel population.
- `src/powerups/unlocks.ts` — unlock machinery to be removed (AC5).
- `src/powerups/choiceReward.ts` / `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — shared reward application for spin outcomes.
- `src/core/gameConfig.ts` — register the wheel scene.
- `src/core/checkpointStore.ts` — remove `unlockedWeapons`; bump `CHECKPOINT_VERSION`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMiniBoss.ts` — exercise the shared wheel/reward path (parity).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/powerups/__tests__/miniBossWheel.test.ts` (new) — tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.4, `docs/BALANCING.md` — documentation updates.

## Related work

- AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH — Mini-boss reward: upgrade-or-unlock + locked pool (current behaviour being replaced).
- AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F — AI bot reward-screen selection (demo auto-select contract to preserve).
- AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF — six-slot permanent loadout accounting (slot pool the wheel reads).
- AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6 — power-up level store (permanent levels/caps applied by the wheel).
- AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 — gym↔game parity (shared modules requirement).
- AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q — hold-full choice overlay (pattern the wheel scene mirrors).

- AH-0MVH87A3L004VOLD — Mini-boss/boss strength scales with player firepower (completed; adjacent balance context for reward power).
- AH-0MVCRKAPL000L68Y — Show current upgrades on the hull-full screen (open; same "player must see what they own" UI concern).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope risk:** celebration VFX/audio for the spin and rebalancing the
  1/5/10/84 split are follow-ups — record as separate work items, not scope.
- **Assumption (cap-aware draws):** when a drawn kind has hit its level cap,
  re-draw a non-capped owned kind; if every owned kind is capped the spin
  grants a fallback (minerals). Confirm during planning.
- **Assumption (mandatory spin):** the wheel always grants something and has
  no skip/decline path (a refusable "reward" recreates the perceived-nothing
  outcome).
- **Risk (unlock removal):** deleting the unlock feature removes a shipped
  progression mechanic; GDD §4.4.4 and the locked-pool docs must be rewritten
  in the same change so no doc promises unlocks. `CHECKPOINT_VERSION` bump
  invalidates existing checkpoints (accepted: pre-release).
- **Risk (resolver/UI drift):** the wedge list and the weighted outcome must
  be derived from the same owned-kind snapshot; the scene must never compute
  probabilities itself.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Scope of unlock rewards.** "The wheel shows icons of power-ups the
  player has; should it fully replace the current upgrade-or-unlock choice
  (removing the run-scoped weapon-unlock feature, its locked-pool options and
  the checkpoint's `unlockedWeapons` field)?" — **Answer (producer, interactive
  reply): Option A — fully replace.** The mini-boss reward becomes purely the
  upgrade wheel; unlock machinery is removed and `CHECKPOINT_VERSION` is
  bumped. Supersedes the options B (locked weapons as wheel outcomes) and C
  (separate secondary unlock offer). Source: producer answer, this intake
  session; recorded as AC5.
- **Q2 — Wheel population and empty-owned fallback.** "Should the wheel show
  **all** owned permanent kinds across the shared 6-slot pool (power-up kinds
  **and** weapon drops), and what happens at a mini-boss defeat when the
  player owns nothing permanent (possible at the level-1 mini-boss)?" —
  **Answer (producer, interactive reply): Option A** — all owned permanent
  kinds; when none are owned, fall back to the existing three-option
  hold-full-style choice so a mini-boss always pays. Options B (power-ups
  only) and C (seed the wheel with base entries) rejected. Source: producer
  answer, this intake session; recorded as AC1 + AC4.
- **Q3 — Wheel visual and weights.** "Should the wheel be 100 literal wedges,
  or a compact wheel (one wedge per owned icon + bonus wedge) whose spin
  outcome is weighted by the 100-slot distribution (1/5/10/84)?" —
  **Answer (producer, interactive reply): Option A** — compact wheel plus
  weighted outcome: legible UI, exact distribution preserved, multi-upgrades
  pick distinct kinds where possible. Options B (literal 100-wedge wheel) and
  C (proportional fixed wheel, accepting granularity loss) rejected. Source:
  producer answer, this intake session; recorded as AC1/AC3.

## Related-work check (duplicate detection)

Duplicate check performed (`wl search "mini-boss reward"`, `wl search
"wheel"`): no overlapping open item found — the closest items
(AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH, AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F, AH-0MVNT2Z89005OPKJ,
AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF) are completed/in-progress parents whose scope this item
extends or replaces; no duplicate.

- **AH-0MVH87A3L004VOLD** – Strength of mini-boss and boss should raise with the fire power of the player (completed)

# Make Phase Shift and wormhole-emergence effects unmistakable

## Problem statement

The improved Phase Shift / wormhole-emergence treatment shipped under
AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S (commits 4267a534, 4b407b66, eafc45b6, c84c1a99, 5b5877e4) is
technically complete and audited, but **the producer reports it is still not
noticeable enough — the effect must be unmistakable**. The intent of the original
epic ("instantly obvious that they are not in their usual state") is therefore not
yet satisfied in practice, even though every written acceptance criterion passed.

Producer feedback (2026-10-25, verbatim): *"These effects are not noticeable
enough, needs to be unmistakable."*

## Users

- **Player (primary):** "As a player, the instant my ship phases out — or enemies
  start materialising out of the wormhole — I want to *know* without looking for
  it. Not a tint I have to hunt for: an unmistakable event."
- **Player (defensive read):** "As a player relying on the automatic Phase Shift, I
  want the activation to read like a system event (a hit, a pulse, a distortion),
  not a subtle colour shift, so I can trust it and time my flying."
- **Developer / maintainer:** "As a developer, I want whatever stronger treatment we
  choose to live once in the shared VFX layer, stay toggleable per layer, and keep
  the gyms and the game pixel-identical."

## Current state (what shipped, and why it reads as subtle)

Screen-wide Phase Shift (`src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts`):

| Layer | Current value |
|---|---|
| Dim overlay | dark blue 0x0a1a33, alpha 0.22 |
| Chromatic split | cyan 0x33ffee / red 0xff3355, **alpha 0.20**, base offset **6 px** (+/-1.5 px, 1.6 s) |
| Alpha flicker | 3 Hz, 25 % depth |
| Colour pulse | 0.75 -> 1.0 cross-fade |
| Activation burst | alpha 0.35 at +/-12 px, 200 ms fade |
| Camera shake | **deliberately none** (producer decision: it read like death juice) |

Per-enemy emergence (`src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` `updateEnemyShimmer`):
ripple burst +0.06 scale / +0.15 alpha over 200 ms, then alpha flicker 0.55-0.85 at
3 Hz, scale pulse 4 %, additive-bloom colour pulse (Phaser 4 `Container`/`Graphics`
have no Tint).

Wormhole ring (`attachWormholeRing`): 0xd9b3ff, r 52 px, 3 px stroke, alpha 0.45,
yoyo scale 0.9-1.15 every 900 ms.

Diagnosis of the shortfall (to be confirmed with the producer): every layer is a
**low-alpha translucent tint at screen-wide scale**, and translucency over a busy
bullet-hell background is perceptually weak. "Unmistakable" most likely needs
*high-contrast, structural* change — distortion, a hard flash, silhouettes, motion —
not just larger alpha values.

## Candidate approaches (producer to choose / amend)

**A — Bigger same-technique (lowest risk, no new rendering technique).**
Split alpha 0.20 -> ~0.45 and offset 6 -> ~14 px; burst alpha 0.35 -> ~0.70 at
+/-28 px over ~320 ms; add a short full-screen brightness flash on activation
(distinct palette from the death flash); add cyan edge/vignette bands during phase
(the defeat-screen vignette technique) so the *frame* changes, not just the objects;
per-enemy alpha flicker range widened (e.g. 0.25-1.0) plus a stroked silhouette
outline per emerging enemy; wormhole ring radius/alpha raised with an open shockwave.

**B — Real screen-space distortion via Phaser camera post-FX (highest impact).**
Use the engine's built-in post-FX pipelines on the main camera while phased: a
short displacement/pixelate wobble on the activation edge, then a sustained subtle
`Bloom`/`Glow` + gentle `Barrel`/`Displacement` wobble, all driven from the same
tunables. This is the genuine "glitch" read and is far more visible than alpha
tints. Caveats: the original epic explicitly scoped shader/render-to-texture work
out; needs a WebGL check + a headless-safe fallback, a measurable perf check, and a
canvas-renderer degradation path. Phaser post-FX state must also be torn down
exactly on the falling edge.

**C — Combination (recommended by the agent, producer decides).**
A for the player + wormhole (cheap, robust) **plus** B's activation-edge distortion
burst only (a ~150-250 ms pixelate/displacement hit), so the *event* is unmistakable
while the *sustained* state stays comfortable.

## Constraints

- **Gym<->game parity** (AGENTS.md): the behaviour lives once in `src/vfx/*` and the
  shared spawn path; `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel` and the combat gyms
  consume the same code. The duplicate-body guard and the gym-parity docs assertion
  must stay green.
- **No camera shake** unless the producer explicitly reverses that decision. (The
  regression test asserting "never shakes" currently encodes it.) If a shake-free
  "punch" is wanted, prefer camera **zoom** punch or post-FX over shake.
- **Seizure safety:** a genuinely unmistakable effect must still avoid rapid strobe.
  If flicker frequency rises, cap it (~<=3-4 Hz for sustained layers) and add an
  explicit accessibility toggle; a reduce-motion option remains a separate item.
- **Per-layer toggles and pure params model** are retained (`PHASE_SHIFT_ENABLE_*`,
  `ENEMY_SHIMMER_ENABLE_*`, `WORMHOLE_RING_ENABLE`, pure `resolve*Params()`).
- **Headless-safe:** no-op without a Phaser render context; unit tests stay
  deterministic.
- **Performance-neutral to near-neutral:** no per-frame allocations; post-FX, if
  chosen, needs a measured cost check on the existing target hardware.
- **Visual distinctness from player-death juice** must be preserved and asserted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Player activation edge is an aggressive, structural glitch: a short camera-filter distortion burst plus a full-screen phase flash plus a wider chromatic surge.
- Player sustained state stays continuously obvious but soft: pulsing vivid split, cyan edge vignette bands, gentle sustained camera filter, no camera shake.
- Exact teardown: the falling edge removes every overlay, tween and camera filter, restoring the camera filter list with no residual state or duplicate layer.
- WebGL capability probe with graceful fallback: filter layers apply only when supported, otherwise degrading to overlay-only layers without throwing.
- Per-enemy emergence is unmistakable per entity: outline silhouette, stronger ripple burst, widened alpha flicker, fully restored when growth ends, no screen-wide overlay.
- Wormhole read: a brighter larger pulsing ring plus a one-shot open shockwave, tracked in wormholeEffects and fully cleared when the wormhole closes.
- Distinctness and parity preserved: visually distinct from player-death juice, never shakes the camera, gym-game parity guards green, headless no-op safe.
- Tests and docs: unit tests cover every new layer, teardown, fallback and the no-shake regression; GDD section 7.2 and code comments document all tunables; the full suite passes.

## Acceptance notes (detail per criterion)

1. **Activation edge (aggressive).** Rising edge fires, in the same frame: a ~150-250 ms camera-filter distortion burst (pixelate + barrel/displacement wobble), a full-screen flash in a phase-shift palette (never the player-death flash palette), and the widened/stronger chromatic-surge overlay pair. Every magnitude is an exported tunable; every layer has its own `PHASE_SHIFT_ENABLE_*` toggle.
2. **Sustained state (soft).** Split alpha/offset raised and slowly oscillating, cyan edge/vignette band layer, gentle sustained filter layer; sustained flicker capped at <=3-4 Hz for seizure safety; no camera shake.
3. **Teardown detail.** A second expiry, a scene `SHUTDOWN` or a re-activation cycle leaves no residual tint, no leaked filter controller, no duplicated layer; pre-existing unrelated camera filters survive untouched.
4. **Fallback detail.** Renderer probe checks the WebGL renderer type and the camera filter list; unsupported renderers get the overlay-only layers with no error storm (headless/canvas tests exercise this path).
5. **Emergence detail.** Driven from the shared spawn path (`updateSpawnAnimation` -> `updateEnemyShimmer`) over the whole `ENEMY_GROWTH_DURATION`; the entity's own alpha/scale/blend state is fully restored when growth ends.
6. **Wormhole detail.** One ring and one shockwave per wormhole; tweens stopped before destroy; registry cleared on close.
7. **Distinctness detail.** The no-shake regression test is retained; the duplicate-body guard (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and the gym-parity docs assertion stay green.
8. **Docs detail.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` section 7.2 plus JSDoc on every new exported constant and helper.

## Producer decisions (2026-10-25)## Producer decisions (2026-10-25)

- **Q1 = C** — combination: approach A (bigger same-technique + frame-level flash/vignette/silhouette) everywhere, **plus** approach B's screen-space distortion for the player path.
- **Q2 = iii** — aggressive on the activation edge, soft for the sustained state.
- **Q3 = no shake** — the no-camera-shake decision stands; the "punch" comes from post-FX/flash layers only. The existing regression test stays.
- **Q4 = ship and iterate** — the epic AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S is **not** held: no dependency edge from the epic to this item; it releases through the normal dev->main gate and this item improves the effect afterwards.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Which approach?** (A) bigger same-technique only; (B) real screen-space post-FX distortion for the player path; (C) combination.
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-25): **C**. Rationale: keep the robust overlay/vignette/silhouette work everywhere and add a genuine distortion read for the player's activation.
- **Q2 — How far may intensity go?** (i) comfortably strong; (ii) aggressive/startling; (iii) aggressive activation edge, soft sustained.
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-25): **iii**. Rationale: the *event* must be unmistakable; the *state* must stay comfortable for the whole phase duration.
- **Q3 — Revisit the no-shake rule?** (i) keep no-shake, use post-FX/flash instead; (ii) allow a short low-intensity shake on the activation edge only.
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-25): **no shake**. Rationale: preserves the established distinctness from player-death juice.
- **Q4 — Release hold for the epic AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S?** hold its release until this lands, or ship and iterate.
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-25): **ship and iterate**. No blocking edge is wired from the epic to this item.

## Technical feasibility note (verified before planning)

Phaser 4.2.1 exposes camera filters (`camera.filters.internal` / `.external`):
`addPixelate`, `addBarrel`, `addGlow`, `addVignette`, `addBlur`, `addParallelFilters`
(bloom), `addDisplacement`, `addColorMatrix`. They are **WebGL only**, so the driver
must probe `scene.game.renderer.type` / `camera.filters` and degrade to the
overlay-only layers otherwise. No post-FX is used anywhere in `src/` today, so this is
a new (but engine-supported) technique.

## Constraints

- **Gym<->game parity** (AGENTS.md): the behaviour lives once in `src/vfx/*` and the
  shared spawn path; `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel` and the combat gyms
  consume the same code. The duplicate-body guard and the gym-parity docs assertion
  must stay green.
- **No camera shake** unless the producer explicitly reverses that decision. (The
  regression test asserting "never shakes" currently encodes it.) If a shake-free
  "punch" is wanted, prefer camera **zoom** punch or post-FX over shake.
- **Seizure safety:** a genuinely unmistakable effect must still avoid rapid strobe.
  If flicker frequency rises, cap it (~<=3-4 Hz for sustained layers) and add an
  explicit accessibility toggle; a reduce-motion option remains a separate item.
- **Per-layer toggles and pure params model** are retained (`PHASE_SHIFT_ENABLE_*`,
  `ENEMY_SHIMMER_ENABLE_*`, `WORMHOLE_RING_ENABLE`, pure `resolve*Params()`).
- **Headless-safe:** no-op without a Phaser render context; unit tests stay
  deterministic.
- **Performance-neutral to near-neutral:** no per-frame allocations; post-FX, if
  chosen, needs a measured cost check on the existing target hardware.
- **Visual distinctness from player-death juice** must be preserved and asserted.

## Acceptance Criteria (draft — finalise after producer answers Q1-Q3)

- **Unmistakable activation read (player).** On the `isPhased` rising edge the
  treatment produces a structural, high-contrast change (not merely a tint): the
  chosen mechanism (A/B/C) fires within the same frame and is perceptible against a
  busy background in a manual play check; magnitudes exported as tunables with
  per-layer toggles.
- **Unmistakable sustained read (player).** While phased, the state remains
  continuously obvious for the whole duration (chosen sustained layer(s) from A
  and/or B), with the no-camera-shake guarantee intact and every layer torn down on
  the falling edge (no residual tint or residual post-FX state).
- **Unmistakable emergence read (enemies).** Each emerging enemy is individually
  obvious as "not solid yet" across its whole `ENEMY_GROWTH_DURATION` window, driven
  from the shared spawn path; the entity's own render state is fully restored when
  growth ends; no screen-wide overlay on the emergence path.
- **Wormhole read.** The open wormhole is clearly the source of the emergence (ring
  and/or column strengthened per the chosen approach), tracked in the existing
  `wormholeEffects` registry and fully cleared on close.
- **No regressions.** Death juice stays visually distinct; the no-shake regression
  holds (unless the producer reverses it, in which case it is updated deliberately);
  gym<->game parity guards pass; headless no-op tests pass.
- **Tests and docs.** Unit tests cover the new tunables/toggles, the new
  layers/mechanism creation + teardown (including post-FX teardown if chosen), and
  the no-shake and headless guarantees. `docs/Game Design Document.md` section 7.2
  and the code comments are updated with the final magnitudes. The full project test
  suite passes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) — magnitudes, new layers, optional
  camera post-FX driver.
- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) — per-enemy treatment, wormhole ring.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — shared driver (post-FX needs a camera).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts` — consume the shared helpers only (no new behaviour).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` section 7.2 — final treatment + tunables.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S** (completed, audited, awaiting release) — the epic that
  delivered the current treatment. This item is `discovered-from:AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S`.
  The producer must decide whether the epic's release is held until this lands.
- AH-0MVD2MXAB004K0V4 — player phase-shift juice (vivid split + burst + shimmer).
- AH-0MVD2N333004VDA9 — per-enemy emergence shimmer.
- AH-0MVD2N6AW0073X5M — wormhole glow/pulse ring.
- AH-0MUJRGWGG0073JWS — original Phase Shift juice module (dim + split, no shake).
- AH-0MUTV7632000ZWCB — end-of-run juice; the defeat glitch-flicker + vignette
  technique is the precedent for approach A's frame-level layers.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: seizure sensitivity / discomfort** — "unmistakable" pushes toward higher
  contrast and faster flicker. Mitigation: cap sustained flicker, keep the aggressive
  part on the short activation edge, keep per-layer toggles, and track a
  reduce-motion accessibility option separately.
- **Risk: post-FX complexity and platform variance** (approach B) — WebGL-only,
  needs canvas fallback, exact teardown, and a perf measurement. Mitigation: fall
  back to approach A layers when post-FX is unavailable.
- **Risk: parity drift** — mitigated by implementing once in the shared VFX layer;
  guards enforce it.
- **Assumption:** the producer's "unmistakable" means *perceptually unavoidable*,
  not necessarily *physically larger* — the chosen mechanism is a producer decision
  (Q1-Q3 above).

# Intake Brief — Mini Boss explosions

**Work item:** AH-0MVOFGB6K003YD0Z (feature, high)
**Headline:** On mini-boss defeat, explode every remaining wave-gating enemy
(escorts plus the mini-boss's live minions) in a staggered sweep, add
`max(0, 30 − n)` extra explosions scattered at random across the scene plus 10
around the mini-boss's death point, and hold the mini-boss reward overlay until
every explosion animation has finished.

**Source request (verbatim):** "When the mini-boss it defeated all remaining
enemies should explode, add an additional 30 - # of enemies explosions
scattered randomly across the scene and 10 around the mini-boss. Do not show
the reward screen until all explosions have completed their animation."

## Problem statement

Defeating a mini-boss currently destroys only the mini-boss body (with its own
boss-scale explosion): surviving escorts and summoned minions stay on the field,
no celebration scatter fires, and the reward overlay opens on the same frame as
the kill — mid-explosion — so the defeat reads as abrupt rather than
celebratory. The operator wants a cascading explosion sweep on the defeat frame,
a short celebratory scatter, and the reward screen held back until the last
burst has finished animating.

## Users

- **Player** — "As a player, when I defeat the mini-boss I want every remaining
  enemy to blow up and an extra barrage of explosions across the screen, so the
  kill feels like a clear victory moment."
- **Player** — "As a player, I want the reward screen to appear only after the
  explosion display has finished, so I don't miss the celebration."
- **Developer/tester (gym)** — "As a tester I want the mini-boss gym's EXPLODE
  button to show the same sweep, so what I verify in the gym is what ships."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Remaining wave-gating enemies explode.** On the mini-boss's lethal
  hit, every live wave-gating enemy is destroyed in a staggered explosion sweep
  that begins on the defeat frame. Scope is **escort ships plus the mini-boss's
  live summoned minions**; non-blocking hazards (`asteroid`, `lane-traffic`, per
  `isNonBlockingHazard`) are **not** swept and remain on the field.
- **AC2 — Extra scattered explosions.** The sweep adds `max(0, 30 − n)` extra
  particle explosions, where `n` is the number of wave-gating enemies swept
  (escorts + minions), placed at positions sampled uniformly at random across
  the playfield, plus exactly **10** explosions clustered around the mini-boss's
  death position captured at destruction. Edge cases are explicit: `n = 0` → 30
  extras; `n = 30` → 0 extras; `n > 30` → 0 extras (never negative, never an
  exception). Total scattered bursts therefore never exceed 30.
- **AC3 — Reward screen waits for the explosions.** The mini-boss reward overlay
  (`MineralChoiceScene`, opened by `PlayScene.openMiniBossReward`) opens only
  after the last explosion burst in the sweep has completed its animation. The
  `miniBossRewardOpen` latch still opens exactly one overlay per defeat, and the
  demo auto-select contract (AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F) still applies after the delay
  (attract mode never stalls).
- **AC4 — Cosmetic-only destruction.** Swept enemies are removed from play but
  award **no score**, drop **no minerals / power-ups / Extra Life**, and emit
  **no kill telemetry**. Wave/level accounting still clears exactly once,
  **after** the sweep: the level advance never fires mid-display and never fires
  twice.
- **AC5 — Game↔gym parity.** `GymMiniBoss`'s EXPLODE path runs the **same**
  shared sweep helper as `PlayScene` (one implementation consumed by both); the
  repo duplicate-body guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and the
  gym-parity docs assertion pass.
- **AC6 — Determinism and meaningful tests.** All random placement/jitter uses
  the run-seeded RNG (no `Math.random()` in the sweep), so a seed replays the
  same display; unit tests cover the count formula at the edges (`n = 0, 1, 29,
  30, 40`), the minion/hazard scope split, and the sweep-completion → overlay
  ordering (overlay does not open before the last burst finishes).
- **AC7 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries**
  (notably GDD §3.3/§4.4.4 and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`).
- **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Shared-code parity:** the sweep lives once in a new shared module under
  `src/scenes/core/` and is consumed by `PlayScene` and `GymMiniBoss` — no
  divergent copy (AGENTS.md "Game Architecture Conventions").
- **Reuse the existing VFX:** explosions go through
  `spawnExplosionParticles` (`src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts`) — same particle
  system, ~400 ms burst lifespan, shared per-kind VFX registry
  (`getExplosionVfxCounts`). No new particle system.
- **No reward of any kind** for swept kills (operator answer Q2 = B + C): this
  is celebration VFX only, so the mini-boss reward remains the single reward
  for the encounter.
- **Ordering:** the reward overlay's `setPaused(true)` would freeze the tween
  animations, so the sweep must be allowed to run and complete before the
  overlay pauses the scene.
- **Minion capture order:** mini-boss minions are owned by the `MiniBoss` entity
  and are currently torn down by `MiniBoss.destroy()` → `_clearMinions()`
  (plain `destroy(true)`, no explosion). The sweep must capture the live minions
  (e.g. `miniBoss.getMinions()`) **before** `miniBoss.destroy()`, otherwise they
  cannot be exploded or counted in `n`.
- **Demo mode** must remain non-blocking: the delayed overlay keeps the existing
  auto-select behaviour.
- **Determinism:** seeded RNG for placement/jitter, per the repo VFX contract.

## Existing state

- `PlayScene._damageMiniBoss` (~L2920): on the lethal hit captures a
  `MiniBossDefeatContext`, calls `miniBoss.destroy()` (which also clears
  minions), fires `_fireMiniBossDefeatHooks` (checkpoint + reward), then replays
  one destruction through the wave state machine with a stale-count
  reconciliation guard.
- `_fireMiniBossDefeatHooks` calls `openMiniBossReward` **synchronously** → the
  overlay launches and `setPaused(true)` runs on the defeat frame.
- Remaining escorts/survivors are not destroyed; minions are silently torn down
  with the boss body. Hazards (`isNonBlockingHazard`) are never wave-accounted.
- `MiniBoss extends Boss`; its own death already plays a boss-scale explosion.
  `BaseEnemy.destroySelf(scale?)` / `playExplosion(scale)` is the shared
  per-enemy explosion seam, and `destroySelf()` marks the entity dead without
  awarding anything — so a cosmetic sweep can reuse it directly.
- `GymMiniBoss` destroys via EXPLODE → `MiniBoss.takeDamage()` →
  `destroySelf()`; it has no reward overlay, so the gym shows the sweep only.
- Kill accounting lives in `PlayScene._onEnemyKilled` (score → drops → wave
  advance); the sweep must **not** call that path (AC4).

## Desired change

Introduce a shared `miniBossDeathSweep` helper (pure planner + thin Phaser
executor) that:

1. collects the sweep targets — live wave-gating enemies (excluding
   `isNonBlockingHazard`) plus the mini-boss's live minions captured before the
   entity is destroyed;
2. staggers their `destroySelf()` explosions over a short window so the sweep
   reads as a cascade (a modest burst scale — enemy-scale, not boss-scale);
3. spawns the `max(0, 30 − n)` random scattered extras plus 10 bursts anchored
   at the mini-boss death position, all drawn through
   `spawnExplosionParticles` with the run-seeded RNG;
4. reports completion (last burst finished) so `PlayScene` then opens the
   mini-boss reward overlay; wave accounting advances once, after the sweep.

`GymMiniBoss`'s EXPLODE button calls the same helper (tests observe the burst
counts and completion).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/miniBossDeathSweep.ts` — **new** shared sweep planner
  (count/placement maths) + Phaser executor + completion callback, with tests.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_damageMiniBoss` (capture minions before
  `destroy()`), `_fireMiniBossDefeatHooks` / `openMiniBossReward` (defer the
  overlay until sweep completion), single deferred wave advance.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMiniBoss.ts` — EXPLODE path consumes the shared sweep.
- `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` — reuse `spawnExplosionParticles` /
  `getExplosionVfxCounts`; add a completion-aware spawn option only if needed.
- `src/entities/MiniBoss.ts` — expose/retain live minions long enough for the
  sweep to explode them (e.g. a read-before-destroy accessor).
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — existing `destroySelf()` / `playExplosion(scale)`
  seams consumed by the sweep (no reward side effects).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — gym destroy seam used by the
  sweep in the gym.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§3.3, §4.4.4),
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — defeat-flow documentation.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts` — parity guards that must keep passing.

## Related work

- AH-0MVCC8XSS007P01Z (completed) — mini-boss epic; this sweep refines its
  defeat behaviour.
- AH-0MVCRBISU006NUN5 (completed) — `PlayScene` mini-boss integration
  (`_damageMiniBoss` defeat path this change extends).
- AH-0MVCRAV3B0069AIJ (completed) — `WaveManager` per-level mini-boss gating
  (the wave-advance-once constraint).
- AH-0MVH85XXZ008INE2 (completed) — mini-boss left-behind graphics; precedent
  for tearing the encounter down cleanly on defeat.
- AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH (completed) — mini-boss reward overlay
  (`openMiniBossReward`, `miniBossRewardOpen`), the overlay this change delays.
- AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F (completed) — reward-overlay demo auto-select; must not
  stall behind the new delay.
- AH-0MVCB6LBE007I6R8 (open) — "Stop firing when boss is destroyed": related
  post-destruction cleanup pattern at the final boss; check for a shared
  "defeat moment" seam rather than duplicating gating logic.
- AH-0MUWZ5HCV0034H44 / AH-0MUTV7632000ZWCB (completed) — staggered
  multi-burst celebration scheduling (`spawnVictoryFireworks`) to mirror.
- AH-0MVJ8TB610098DSY (open) — "Explosions sould be explosions": image-based
  explosion rendering; overlaps the VFX module but is orthogonal (visual
  quality vs defeat-sweep behaviour).
- AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V (completed) — the shared particle explosion module this
  change reuses.

Duplicate check: performed (keywords "explosions", "mini-boss", "reward
screen", "chain explosion") — **no overlapping completed item found**; the
nearest items (VFX quality AH-0MVJ8TB610098DSY, final-boss victory fireworks
AH-0MUWZ5HCV0034H44 / AH-0MUTV7632000ZWCB) do not cover a mini-boss-defeat
explosion sweep.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** applies to the **mini-boss defeat only**. Extending the
  sweep to the final boss or ordinary wave clears is separate work (record as
  discovered work items, not scope).
- **Particle budget:** up to 40 bursts in a short window. Mitigation: extra and
  anchored bursts use a modest enemy-scale size/scale and a reduced particle
  count; the sweep is bounded by `max(0, 30 − n) + 10 + n ≤ 40` bursts.
- **Double-advance risk:** `_damageMiniBoss` already has a stale-count
  reconciliation that can replay `onEnemyDestroyed`; sweeping enemies changes
  the alive count, so tests must assert the level advance fires exactly once,
  after the sweep.
- **Minion teardown ordering** (see Constraints) — capture before destroy, or
  minions vanish without exploding and `n` is under-counted.
- **Pause ordering:** the overlay's pause freezes tweens; completion must be
  driven by real tween completion (or an explicit timer derived from burst
  lifespan + stagger), not by a frame count that could be frozen.
- **Assumption:** the 10 mini-boss bursts are anchored at the death position
  captured at destruction (same discipline as the victory fireworks anchor), not
  at the entity's (already destroyed) live coordinates.
- **Assumption:** "scattered randomly across the scene" means uniformly sampled
  within the playfield inset by the burst radius, so no explosion is clipped
  entirely off-screen. If the producer expects the full screen edge-to-edge,
  only the inset constant changes.
- **Assumption:** the sweep is a visual-only celebration; the mini-boss reward
  remains the only reward for the encounter (operator Q2 = B + C).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Per entry: question, answer, answering party, evidence.

- **Q1 (scope of "all remaining enemies")** — "Which live entities count as
  'all remaining enemies' and explode on the sweep: (a) everything alive on the
  field — escort ships, mini-boss-summoned minions, and hazards (asteroids, lane
  traffic); (b) wave-gating enemies only (escorts + minions, exclude hazards);
  or (c) escort ships only (exclude minions and hazards)?"
  — **Answer (operator): "1. B"** — wave-gating enemies only: escort ships plus
  the mini-boss's live minions; hazards (asteroids, lane traffic) are excluded
  and survive. Recommended option was (b); operator selected (b). Source:
  interactive reply. Research: `PlayScene.spawned` holds one entry per live
  entity including hazards; `isNonBlockingHazard`
  (`src/scenes/core/waveTimeout.ts`) is the shared hazard classifier, and
  `MiniBoss.getMinions()` exposes the entity-owned minions.
- **Q2 (kill semantics)** — "Should sweep-destroyed enemies be real kills — (a)
  full shared kill path (score, mineral/power-up/Extra-Life drops, telemetry)
  with wave-advance batched to sweep end; (b) cosmetic explosions only —
  enemies removed visually, no score/drops; or (c) destroyed without any reward
  or telemetry?"
  — **Answer (operator): "2. B + C"** — treat as (b) cosmetic explosions only
  **and** (c) no reward or telemetry: enemies are removed visually with their
  explosion VFX, and award no score, no mineral/power-up/Extra-Life drops and no
  kill telemetry (wave bookkeeping still updates so the level completes). Source:
  interactive reply. Recommended option was (a); operator overrode it with
  B + C. Research: `PlayScene._onEnemyKilled` is the reward-bearing path and
  must **not** be used by the sweep; `BaseEnemy.destroySelf()` marks the entity
  dead and plays its explosion only, so it is the correct seam.
- **Q3 (count formula edges)** — "With n remaining enemies, the spec says
  `30 − n` extra scattered explosions. When n ≥ 30 (or 0), what should happen:
  (a) clamp extra at 0 — total scattered bursts = `max(30, n)` from enemy bursts
  + extras, plus the fixed 10 at the mini-boss; (b) always fire at least 30
  scattered extras regardless of n; or (c) always fire exactly 30 scattered
  extras on top of the n enemy bursts (total `30 + n`)?"
  — **Answer (operator): "3. A"** — clamp the extra count at 0:
  `extras = max(0, 30 − n)`, so `n = 0` gives 30 extras and `n ≥ 30` gives none;
  the 10 mini-boss-anchored bursts are always additional. Source: interactive
  reply. Recommended option was (a); operator selected (a). Research: at a clean
  defeat `n` is usually small (escorts cleared first), but carry-over survivors
  and minions can push `n` higher, so the clamp keeps the display bounded
  (`total bursts ≤ n + max(0, 30 − n) + 10 ≤ 40`).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVBMESIE003YQ68** – AI should focus fire on the boss (open)
- **AH-0MVCRBISU006NUN5** – PlayScene mini-boss integration (completed)

- `README.md` — matched: 0mvcc8xss007p01z, 0mvj8u79v0056i2f, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+425 more)

- **AC1 — New setup fields are parsed and validated.** `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` covers `setup.player.weaponLevels`, `setup.bossHitsRemaining` and `setup.mineralReward`: accepted shapes parse; wrong shapes raise the documented error codes; normalisation yields documented defaults; re-normalising a normalised setup is idempotent (deep-equal).

- **AC3 — Applier behaviour is specified.** `src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.test.ts` asserts with a fake player that `player.weaponLevels: { rapid: 3 }` produces three permanent `equipWeapon('rapid', true)` calls (level N == N permanent grants), that `player.weapons` still grants level 1, and that a forced `mineralReward` selects the named reward instead of a random one.

# Shared wormhole-transit destination seam, consumed by all four spawn sites

Parent: AH-0MVP5IGX5005XTVV (AC4, and prerequisite for AC1). **Pure refactor: behaviour must not
change in any scene.**

## Goal / user story

As a gameplay developer, I want the wormhole-transit destination resolution defined exactly once,
so that the game and every gym consume the same "autonomous-mover exemption → orbital live slot →
grid-slot/offset fallback" rule, and a re-introduced copy fails the suite.

## Problem

The resolver is currently inlined three times:

- `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1647`) — the reference behaviour
  (`formationSlot` seam + `marchState` base + `driftX`).
- `GymFormationScene._spawnFormation` (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts:1755`) — same
  rule, portal-based base, no march.
- `GymLevel.spawnWave` (`src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts:299`) — a **divergent** copy that returns the
  grid slot and therefore reproduces the reported "Phaser spawns in a line then snaps" symptom.
- `GymBoss` minion spawn (`src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts:274`) — no resolver at all (in-place).

The repo-wide duplicate-body guard (`EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS` in
`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) does not cover this seam, which is why the third
copy could drift unnoticed.

## Desired change

1. New module `src/scenes/core/spawnTransit.ts` exporting **one** resolver, e.g.
   `resolveSpawnTransitTarget(...)`, which takes the narrow structural inputs it needs and returns
   `{ x, y }` or `undefined` (meaning "no transit — spawn in place"):
   - the entity (read structurally for `autonomousPositioning` and optional `formationSlot`);
   - the base position for this frame (march base when the wave is a march block, else
     `startX + driftX`, `startY`);
   - the formation `offset` and the group `spacingX` / `spacingY`.
   The resolver owns the rule only — it must not import Phaser, must not read scene fields, and must
   not mutate the entity.
2. Consume it at **all four** spawn sites. Each site keeps its own *base* computation (the game's
   `marchState`, the formation gym's portal, the level gym's launched drift, the boss's in-place
   exemption) — that is scene structure, not the rule.
3. `GymLevel` consumes the seam with **unchanged** behaviour in this item (it will still pass its
   grid-slot base, because it has no march/formation-slot wiring yet); the behaviour fix lands in
   the follow-up `GymLevel` parity item. This keeps this item a verifiable no-op refactor.
4. Register the resolver in `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS` in
   `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` with the canonical definer path, and extend the
   guard fixture so a re-introduced copy is proven to fail (the guard already has a
   "detects a re-introduced duplicate" describe block to extend).

## Implementation guidance

- Keep the ordering of the existing rule exactly: **autonomous → orbital live slot → grid offset**.
  The orbital branch must call `formationSlot.call(entity, baseX, baseY)` so the entity's own
  geometry stays authoritative (AH-0MVF4P31M0033RAC, AH-0MVEXVME1004SIIS).
- Preserve every existing comment's intent by moving the rationale into the new module's header
  (the "never appear in a line then snap onto the ring" reason) and leaving short pointers at the
  four call sites.
- Prefer a structural input type over importing entity classes, so the module stays pure and the
  gyms can pass their own shapes.
- Do not "fix" the `GymLevel` behaviour here; the red-before tests from the parity-test item must
  still fail after this item lands.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — `src/scenes/core/spawnTransit.ts` exists, is Phaser-free (importable in a node-only
  unit test), and defines the transit destination rule exactly once.
- [ ] AC2 — `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel` and `GymBoss` all resolve their transit
  destination through that single helper; no site re-implements the orbital/autonomous/offset
  branch chain.
- [ ] AC3 — The helper is registered in `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS` in
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, the single-definer guard passes, and the
  guard's duplicate-detection fixture covers the new helper.
- [ ] AC4 — Unit tests for the new helper cover: autonomous mover → `undefined`; orbital entity →
  live `formationSlot` result (including a slot that differs from the grid slot); non-orbital
  entity → grid slot from base + offset × spacing; march base vs drift base input handling.
- [ ] AC5 — Every pre-existing test passes unchanged (no behaviour change): scene behaviour is

1. **Schema.** Extend the scene config so a gym entry can carry its scenario parameters (enemy
   roster, formation, launched level, toggles) alongside the existing common setup fields
